messages.author: 000953defc4b3692
messages.subject: oSCR.parfit() error message
parts:
Hi group,

I had the multi-session models successfully runnig with oSCR.fit(). However it took forever for a model to converge probably because I have 6 sessions. So instead I was trying to use oSCR.parfit() but it didn't seem to work. Attached is the workspace containing my objects. Below are my codes and the error message:

mods<-make.mods(density= c(~1,~session),
                detection = c(~1,~session,~sex),
                sigma = c(~1,~sex),
                cost = c(~1,~d2rd))
data<-list(sf=sf, ss=ss, cs=cs)
par.mod<-oSCR.parfit(mods=mods, data=data, ncores=4)
Error in { : task 1 failed - "object 'buffer' not found"

Does anyone have suggestions on at least how many cores are needed to run this type of models efficiently (ex. one model converge in <1hr)?
Also in R-help of oSCR.parfit() indicated that feeding starting values are not done yet. I did need to calculate starting values ahead of time with oSCR.fit(...getStarts= T) to get the models running. Does it mean that oSCR.parfit() won't work for my models anyway?

Any comments are appreciated. Thanks.

Tricia

messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: Re: oSCR.parfit() error message
parts:
Hi Tricia, 

The parfit option will not education the time for a single model, but rather, it fits multiple _models_ in parallel. Sometimes these models, especially the multi-session models, can take some time to fit, and more especially if you have many state-space points.

Providing good starting values can make a big difference - the getStarts=T option will return a list with the order of the parameters and the default values used as a guide for providing a vector of starting values.

Setting the trimS argument to a value ~the mmdm can speed things up (this sets the distance limit to localize the evaluation of potential activity centers - be you should test for sensitivity to that like you would the state space buffer.

Finally, the assymetric space use models that compute non-Euclidean distances can take a while as there is a lot going on under the hood (gDistances Dijkstra's algoritmn calculation). Unfortunately that's just the way it is.

Protip: press play on models in the evening so when you wake up models have finished and time taken is less of an issue 😉

Chris

messages.author: 58a62321f08f30f8
messages.subject: RE: oSCR.parfit() error message
parts:
Hi Tricia,

 

I think I tracked down the ‘buffer’ argument issue. It appears to be related to whether or not you provide a state-space object (called an ssDF ‘stat-space dataframe’). If an ssDF is not provided, then one is created under the hood using the make.ssDF() function that requires a buffer and a resolution value. I am working on some updates at the moment so I will add a fix to this so it uses mmdm to set the buffer and resolution. I will also add the caveat that one should think carefully about defining the state-space; in fact, this is one of the reasons oSCR places so much emphasis on making the state-space a user defined object.

 

But, in response to your initial buffer related question, add the state-space to ‘data’ object, e.g.:

 

Data is a list with the required oSCR.fit objects: data$sf = scrFrame, data$ss = ssDF, data$cs = costDF

 

Hope that helps!

 

Chris
